copy.title: Playlist & press pitch
copy.body: Glass Hours is hazy, synth-washed dream pop about leaving a small town, sung over drum machines and tape-warped guitars. It will suit listeners of TV Girl and Weyes Blood, and sits alongside Alexandra Savior, Soccer Mommy and Jay Som. The core taste signals are dream pop, lo-fi and shoegaze, and the same listeners follow Japanese Breakfast, Beach House, Mazzy Star and Cigarettes After Sex. For playlists built around late-night, intimate indie, it is a natural fit.

copy.title: Who it's for
copy.body: The audience over-indexes female (0.36) and skews young: ≤24 at +0.13, 25–29 at +0.09, and 35–44 at +0.16, while 45–54 sits at -0.57. Their taste descriptors are dream pop, lo-fi, shoegaze, indie pop and psychedelic. They also love Lost in Translation, Frances Ha and Lady Bird, watch Somebody Somewhere and PEN15, and listen to Song Exploder. Seattle and Los Angeles are strongholds; Portland, Boston, Austin and San Jose are emerging. They shop at Urban Outfitters, Free People and Madewell, which suggests brand-adjacent channels. This is aggregate taste, not a forecast.
